gi18_uganda.topic: Documented alternatives to Palestine: Der Judenstaat, East Africa, territorialism, Birobidzhan

claims.text: Herzl, The Jewish State (1896): 'Shall we choose Palestine or Argentine?' ... 'We shall take what is given us.'

A Soviet resolution of 28 March 1928 entrusted Komzet with settlement of Birobidzhan; immigration began April 1928; on 7 May 1934 the Birobidzhan district was made the Jewish Autonomous District (Region).

1939: EJ (Lvavi/Redlich) gives 13,291 Jews (18.57% of the total); Weinberg gives 'just less than 18,000' of about 109,000 inhabitants (figures conflict). Postwar peak about 20,000 at end of 1948, 'the largest ever'; 14,269 (8.8%) in 1959; 11,452 in 1970; 'no more than several thousand' of more than 200,000 in the early 1990s.

Reasons for failure per the encyclopedias: remoteness, harsh climate and marshland, poor infrastructure, limited opportunities, purges of 1936-38 and from 1948; more than half of 1928-33 arrivals left; Khrushchev in 1958 called the settlement 'a failure'. Yiddish was an official language alongside Russian.

gi18_dependency.topic: 1948 as contingent: the 1947 vote margin and the ICJ referral votes

claims.text: Shindler: abstentions and absentees did not count toward the required two-thirds majority; the Ad Hoc Committee vote gave the Zionists a majority but not a two-thirds one; Aranha agreed a three-day postponement; the outcome was 'a close-run thing' and Israel's emergence 'was never inevitable'; Stalin hoped to replace the British in the region; the US recognised Israel in 11 minutes.

Ad Hoc Committee, 24 Nov 1947: Sub-Committee II's proposal to seek ICJ advisory opinions failed: questions 1-7 voted together 18 for, 25 against, 11 abstentions; question 8 (competence to enforce partition) 20 for, 21 against, 13 abstentions.

The eighth question asked whether the UN or any member state was competent to enforce, or recommend the enforcement of, a partition plan adopted without the consent of the inhabitants of Palestine; the committee rejected Sub-Committee 2's unitary-state resolution and adopted Sub-Committee 1's partition plan.

gi18_legitimacy.topic: Legitimacy arguments: Palestinian charters, ICJ 2024, recognition, Arab Peace Initiative, Resolution 194

claims.text: Palestinian National Charter (July 1968), Art. 19: 'The partition of Palestine in 1947 and the establishment of the state of Israel are entirely illegal' ... 'because they were contrary to the will of the Palestinian people' and inconsistent with UN Charter principles, 'particularly the right to self-determination.' Art. 20: the Balfour Declaration and the Mandate 'are deemed null and void'.

Palestinian Declaration of Independence (Algiers, 15 Nov 1988): despite the 'historical injustice' of displacement and denial of self-determination following Resolution 181, 'that resolution nevertheless continues to attach conditions to international legitimacy' guaranteeing Palestinian sovereignty.
The 1988 declaration was proclaimed by Arafat at the 19th PNC in Algiers; 75 states recognised by mid-December 1988, 93 by February 1989.

As of 23 September 2025, 157 of 193 UN member states recognised the State of Palestine (81%); the UK announced recognition on 21 September 2025 and France and others at UNGA 80; Palestine has been a non-member observer state since 2012.

ICJ, 19 July 2024 (press release 2024/57): seeking 'to acquire sovereignty over an occupied territory' is contrary to the prohibition of the use of force; Israel's 'assertion of sovereignty and its annexation of certain parts of the territory' 'constitute a violation of the prohibition of the acquisition of territory by force'; Israel 'is not entitled to sovereignty over ... any part of the Occupied Palestinian Territory'; 'Nor can Israel's security concerns override the principle of the prohibition of the acquisition of territory by force'; the Palestinian people 'has been deprived of its right to self-determination over a long period'; the illegality 'relates to the entirety of the Palestinian territory occupied by Israel in 1967'.

IDI analysis: continued presence unlawful 11-4 (Sebutinde, Tomka, Abraham, Aurescu dissenting); cease settlement and evacuate settlers 14-1; non-recognition by states 12-3; the opinion 'is not legally binding on Israel or other states'; the Court gave Israel's security concerns little weight; Israel had filed a brief position paper asking the Court to decline without addressing the substantive claims.

Resolution 194, para. 11: 'the refugees wishing to return to their homes and live at peace with their neighbours should be permitted to do so at the earliest practicable date' and compensation paid for property of those choosing not to return; adopted 11 December 1948.

Arab Peace Initiative (Beirut, March 2002): 'Full Israeli withdrawal from all the territories occupied since 1967', a just solution to the refugee problem per Resolution 194, a Palestinian state with 'East Jerusalem as its capital'; in return the Arab states would 'Consider the Arab-Israeli conflict ended', sign a peace agreement and 'Establish normal relations with Israel'.
